key_insight: Different disciplines are converging on a unified view of what it takes for systems to act physically and intelligently — moving the focus from prediction and simulation to embodied, materially grounded agency.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of a unified framework and vocabulary for embodied intelligence and 'physical AI', bridging gaps between simulation-heavy ML and the realities of sensors, actuators, materials and real-world interaction.
method: Conceptual synthesis of frameworks across disciplines (robotics, control, cognitive science, materials, ML).
Proposes a high-level taxonomy linking embodiment, sensing, actuation, control and learning to define Physical AI.
Outlines a research agenda and evaluation criteria to move from simulation to real-world, hardware-aware AI systems.
impact: Helps practitioners prioritize hardware–software co-design, real-world evaluation, and cross-disciplinary metrics — accelerating robust, deployable intelligent agents that operate in physical environments.
visual_elements: Venn/convergence diagram showing overlap of disciplines (ML, robotics, materials, control).
Pipeline graphic: perception → representation → decision/control → actuation in the real world.
Taxonomy/roadmap poster with key components, challenges and research milestones for Physical AI.
Side-by-side comparison chart: simulated performance vs physical-world outcomes and failure modes.
paper_title: From embodied intelligence to physical AI
